title.zh: 赌场管制（赌场博彩行为）条例 2009
title.en: Casino Control (Conduct of Casino Gambling) Regulations 2009
title.orig: Casino Control (Conduct of Casino Gambling) Regulations 2009
title.vi: Quy chế Kiểm soát sòng bạc (Thực hiện hoạt động cờ bạc tại sòng bạc) 2009
title.th: ข้อบังคับการควบคุมคาสิโน (การดำเนินการพนันในคาสิโน) 2009

completenessNote: 全文，共 21 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。

chapter.en: PART I PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Citation and commencement

text.en:
1. These Regulations may be cited as the Casino Control (Conduct of Casino Gambling) Regulations 2009 and shall come into operation on 4th December 2009.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART I PRELIMINARY

heading.en: Definitions

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: When casino chips and chip purchase vouchers may be issued or redeemed

text.en:
3. Casino Chips and chip purchase vouchers may only be issued and redeemed during the hours of operation of a casino.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: Payment for casino chips

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: Payment for chip purchase vouchers

text.en:
5. A casino operator must not issue, or cause or permit to be issued, any chip purchase voucher to any patron unless the chip purchase voucher is paid for to the value of the chip purchase voucher by one or more of the following methods of payment:
(a)by direct debit from the amount standing to the credit of the patron’s deposit account or cheque cashing account with the casino operator;
(b)by an exchange of chip purchase vouchers issued by the casino operator; or
(c)by such other mode of payment as the Authority may approve.

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: Limit on casino chips issued in exchange for casino chips of another casino operator

text.en:
6.—(1) A casino operator must not issue, or cause or permit to be issued to any patron, casino chips paid for in casino chips of another casino operator equal to or exceeding an aggregate value of $10,000 in a single business day.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) In this regulation, “business day” means a 24-hour period which constitutes a normal business day of a casino, being the same period by which the casino keeps its books and records for business and accounting purposes.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: Transaction at cage

text.en:
7. A casino operator who issues casino chips paid for in casino chips of another casino operator must do so only at a cage.
[S 285/2019 wef 04/04/2019]
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: Redemption of casino chips or chip purchase vouchers

chapter.en: PART II ISSUANCE, REDEMPTION AND USE OF CASINO CHIPS AND CHIP PURCHASE VOUCHERS

heading.en: Casino chips to be used only for casino gambling or tips in casino premises

text.en:
9.—(1) Casino Chips issued by a casino operator may be used by a patron only for ––
(a)casino gambling; or
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)the giving of tips or gratuities to any person employed within the casino premises for any service provided by such person in the ordinary course of his duties.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Any person who uses casino chips for any purpose other than the purposes allowed under paragraph (1) shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $10,000 or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or to both.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III CONDUCT OF CASINO GAMBLING AT TABLES, ON GAMING MACHINES AND USING GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Dealing and shuffling of playing cards

text.en:
10.—(1) Subject to paragraph (2), the playing cards used by a casino operator for any casino gambling must —
(a)prior to each use, have been shuffled using an electronic shuffler and not manually shuffled; and
(b)be dealt from a card shoe or other device or equipment approved by the Authority.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) The Authority may, on the application of a casino operator or an applicant for a casino licence, waive any or all of the requirements in paragraph (1) for any segment of casino patrons, designated gaming area or approved casino gambling, subject to such conditions as the Authority may impose.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III CONDUCT OF CASINO GAMBLING AT TABLES, ON GAMING MACHINES AND USING GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Placing of wagers on casino gambling at tables

text.en:
11.—(1) Subject to paragraph (2), a wager on any approved casino gambling conducted at a table must be made by casino chips and, if applicable, one or more match play coupons.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) A casino operator must not accept any wager on any approved casino gambling conducted at a table ––
(a)placed on behalf of a patron who is not present in person at the table by another person, or placed by a patron who is not so present using any communication device or equipment;
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)placed otherwise than by means of casino chips issued by the casino operator; or
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)made without any casino chips at the table, unless otherwise provided in the approved rules.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) [Deleted by S 51/2013 wef 31/01/2013]
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III CONDUCT OF CASINO GAMBLING AT TABLES, ON GAMING MACHINES AND USING GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Placing of wagers by proxy on gaming machines and gaming programs

text.en:
11A. A casino operator must take all reasonable steps to ensure that the casino operator does not allow any wager to be placed on a gaming machine or using a gaming program —
(a)by another person on behalf of a patron who is not present in person at the casino; or
(b)by a patron who is not so present using any communication device or equipment.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III CONDUCT OF CASINO GAMBLING AT TABLES, ON GAMING MACHINES AND USING GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Refusal of wagers

text.en:
12.—(1) Without prejudice to regulation 18(1)(d), a licensed special employee of a casino operator conducting any approved casino gambling must refuse a wager from a patron if ––
(a)the licensed special employee knows that a patron is incapable of making a decision in relation to a wager by reason of his state of intoxication, or has reasonable doubts as to the patron’s ability to do so; or
(b)the wager is placed otherwise than in accordance with the approved rules.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Without prejudice to paragraph (1), a licensed special employee of a casino operator conducting any approved casino gambling may refuse a wager from a patron if the licensed special employee knows or reasonably suspects that the patron is committing or has committed an offence under the Act or any other written law in relation to the patron’s participation in the approved casino gambling.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) A refusal of a wager under paragraph (1)(a) or (2) must be done prior to the closing of bets as determined by the approved rules.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) Upon any refusal of a wager under paragraph (1) or (2), the licensed special employee must remove the wager from the table and return it to the patron.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART III CONDUCT OF CASINO GAMBLING AT TABLES, ON GAMING MACHINES AND USING GAMING PROGRAMS

heading.en: Winnings to be paid in casino chips

text.en:
13. Winnings on any approved casino gambling must be paid to a patron only in casino chips, unless otherwise provided in the approved rules.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Payment of winnings in full

text.en:
14. A casino operator must pay every patron who wins a wager on any casino game or other form of casino gambling the patron’s winnings in full without deduction of any commission or fee, unless otherwise provided in the rules of the casino game or other form of casino gambling.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Refund of wagers and recovery of winnings when casino gambling declared void

text.en:
15.—(1) A casino operator must declare any casino gambling void if there is any malfunction or fault in, or interruption in the operation of, any part of any gaming machine, gaming program or other gaming equipment that affects the outcome of the casino gambling.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Without prejudice to paragraph (1), a casino operator may declare any casino gambling void if ––
(a)there is a force majeure event that disrupts the casino gambling;
(b)the casino operator knows or reasonably suspects that a patron is committing or has committed an offence under the Act or any other written law in such a manner as may affect the outcome of the casino gambling; or
(c)the approved rules provide for other circumstances under which the casino gambling may be declared void and the declaration is done under those circumstances.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) If any casino gambling is declared void under paragraph (1) or (2), the casino operator must ––
(a)clearly notify every patron participating in the casino gambling that the casino gambling has been declared void; and
(b)refund all wagers made on the casino gambling.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) Where any casino gambling is declared void under paragraph (1) or (2) (except on the ground of a force majeure event under paragraph (2)(a)), the casino operator may, in addition, recover the winnings of any or all patrons from the casino gambling, if ––
(a)there is clear information provided to the players participating in the casino gambling or displayed prominently in the casino concerning the circumstances under which, and the means by which, winnings will be recovered when the casino gambling is declared void; and
(b)the recovery of winnings is done in accordance with the information in sub-paragraph (a).
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(5) In paragraph (2)(a), “force majeure event” includes ––
(a)fire or flood;
(b)an act of God;
(c)an act of war;
(d)strikes, lock-outs or stoppages or restraints of labour;
(e)riots or civil commotions; or
(f)any other event beyond the control of the casino operator that makes the continuation of the casino gambling impossible.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Patrons to be notified of closure or stoppage of table, gaming machine or gaming program

text.en:
16.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), a casino operator must ensure that reasonable notice is given to patrons before the closure or stoppage of any table, gaming machine or gaming program.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Without limiting the generality of paragraph (1), reasonable notice may be given by ––
(a)displaying a notice of the impending stoppage of a gaming machine or gaming program on the screen of the gaming machine or the electronic device (other than a gaming machine) on which the gaming program is used (as the case may be) for a reasonable period of time before the stoppage of the gaming machine or gaming program, as the case may be; or
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)notifying patrons (orally or otherwise) at a table prior to the commencement of the last round of play before the closure of the table.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) A casino operator may close or stop a table, gaming machine or gaming program without notice where it has reasonable cause to believe that the closure is necessary ––
(a)in the interests of public or private safety;
(b)to ensure that casino gambling is conducted honestly; or
(c)to maintain, repair or otherwise deal immediately with any table, gaming machine, gaming program or other gaming equipment to ensure the security and integrity of casino gambling.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) In this regulation, “closure” and “stoppage”, in relation to a table, gaming machine or gaming program, does not include a momentary stoppage of play from which the play can be resumed at the stage it was stopped.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Casino gambling by intoxicated persons prohibited

text.en:
17. A casino operator must not permit a person who is in a state of intoxication to participate in any casino gambling.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Assistance to patrons

text.en:
17A.—(1) A casino operator must —
(a)display prominently in the casino a notice informing patrons where a copy of the approved rules for each approved casino gambling may be inspected;
(b)display prominently in the casino —
(i)the information concerning those rules, the mode of payment of winning wagers and the payout odds of each winning wager; and
(ii)any other information to the player that the Authority directs; and
(c)display prominently at each table or location related to the participation in any form of casino gambling, a sign indicating the permissible minimum and maximum wagers pertaining to the form of casino gambling.
(2) A casino operator must allow a patron to inspect a copy of the approved rules for any approved casino gambling on request.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]

chapter.en: PART IV GENERAL

heading.en: Duties of licensed special employees in relation to conduct of casino gambling

text.en:
18.—(1) A licensed special employee must not ––
(a)advise a patron how to participate in any casino gambling, except to explain the approved rules or to ensure the patron’s compliance with the relevant approved rules;
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(b)by himself or in conjunction with any other person, corruptly solicit or receive, or agree to receive, any tip, gratuity, consideration or other benefit for himself or for any other person as an inducement to or a reward for improperly influencing the outcome of any casino gambling;
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(c)accept casino chips for any purpose other than those set out in regulation 9(1); or
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(d)permit a patron to participate in any casino gambling if the patron is in a state of intoxication.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(2) Every licensed special employee authorised to issue, exchange or redeem casino chips or chip purchase vouchers must do so only in accordance with regulations 3 to 8.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3) Every licensed special employee authorised to conduct casino gambling must ––
(a)deal and shuffle playing cards only in accordance with regulation 10;
(b)accept, refuse or refund wagers only in accordance with regulations 11, 12 and 15(3);
(c)pay or recover winnings only in accordance with regulations 13, 14 and 15(4);
(d)declare any casino gambling void if any of the circumstances mentioned in regulation 15(1) occurs; and
[S 285/2019 wef 04/04/2019]
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(e)give notice of the closure of a table, gaming machine or gaming program in accordance with regulation 16(1) or (2) where necessary.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(3A) Every licensed special employee authorised to conduct casino gambling must not declare any casino gambling void if none of the circumstances mentioned in regulation 15(1) or (2) occurs.
[S 285/2019 wef 04/04/2019]
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
(4) It shall be a condition of a special employee licence that the licensed special employee comply with —
(a)paragraph (1) in every case; and
(b)where applicable to the licensed special employee, paragraphs (2), (3) and (3A).
[S 285/2019 wef 04/04/2019]
(5) A licensed special employee who contravenes a condition of a special employee licence applicable to him under this regulation shall be liable to disciplinary action under section 93 of the Act.
[S 635/2026 wef 21/09/2026]
